The femo + m- collocation also occurs with rfy in the supplied glossary. This is evidence of a shared body-part construction, not proof of a particular contact origin or unrestricted synonymy.

II mtarak- and III matrak-/matrək- remain distinct, as in round 1. The packet provides no additional secure stem-I example or evidence to settle whether round-1 kturki is productive I. The learned identity discussion in Jan 3.15/169 supplies an abstract II object, not a semantic II/III contrast.
